actions.name: conduct reconnaissance operations to gather victim identity information
actions.description: The actors likely conduct reconnaissance operations to gather victim identity information.

actions.name: gain persistent access to victim networks via brute force
actions.description: The actors gain persistent access to victim networks frequently via brute force.

actions.name: use brute force such as password spraying and MFA push bombing to compromise user accounts
actions.description: Since October 2023, Iranian actors have used brute force, such as password spraying, and multi-factor authentication (MFA) ‘push bombing’ to compromise user accounts and obtain access to organizations.

actions.name: modify MFA registrations to enable persistent access
actions.description: The actors frequently modified MFA registrations, enabling persistent access.

actions.name: perform discovery on compromised networks to obtain additional credentials and information
actions.description: The actors performed discovery on the compromised networks to obtain additional credentials and identify other information that could be used to gain additional points of access.

actions.name: use valid user and group email accounts obtained via brute force to access Microsoft 365, Azure, and Citrix systems
actions.description: The actors use valid user and group email accounts, frequently obtained via brute force such as password spraying, to obtain initial access to Microsoft 365, Azure, and Citrix systems.

actions.name: send MFA push notifications to legitimate users to gain access
actions.description: In some cases where push notification-based MFA was enabled, the actors send MFA requests to legitimate users seeking acceptance of the request, known as MFA fatigue or push bombing.

actions.name: register their devices with MFA using compromised user accounts
actions.description: Once the threat actors gain access to an account, they frequently register their devices with MFA to protect their access to the environment via the valid account.

actions.name: leverage compromised user’s open MFA registration to register actor’s own device
actions.description: In two confirmed compromises, the actors leveraged a compromised user’s open registration for MFA to register the actor’s own device to access the environment.

actions.name: use self-service password reset tool to reset expired passwords and register MFA through Okta
actions.description: In another confirmed compromise, the actors used a self-service password reset (SSPR) tool associated with a public facing Active Directory Federation Service (ADFS) to reset the accounts with expired passwords and then registered MFA through Okta for compromised accounts without MFA already enabled.

actions.name: conduct activity using a VPN service
actions.description: The actors frequently conduct their activity using a virtual private network (VPN) service.

actions.name: use Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for lateral movement
actions.description: The actors use Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for lateral movement.

actions.name: use Microsoft Word to open PowerShell to launch the RDP binary mstsc.exe
actions.description: In one instance, the actors used Microsoft Word to open PowerShell to launch the RDP binary mstsc.exe.

actions.name: use open-source tools and methodologies to gather more credentials
actions.description: The actors likely use open-source tools and methodologies to gather more credentials.

actions.name: perform Kerberos Service Principal Name (SPN) enumeration and receive Kerberos tickets
actions.description: The actors performed Kerberos Service Principal Name (SPN) enumeration of several service accounts and received Kerberos tickets.

actions.name: use Active Directory Microsoft Graph API PowerShell application to perform directory dump of all AD accounts
actions.description: In one instance, the actors used the Active Directory (AD) Microsoft Graph Application Program Interface (API) PowerShell application likely to perform a directory dump of all AD accounts.

actions.name: import DomainPasswordSpray.ps1 tool likely to conduct password spraying
actions.description: The actors imported the tool DomainPasswordSpray.ps1, which is openly available on GitHub, likely to conduct password spraying.

actions.name: use Cmdkey /list command likely to display usernames and credentials
actions.description: The actors also used the command Cmdkey /list, likely to display usernames and credentials.

actions.name: attempt impersonation of the domain controller likely by exploiting Netlogon vulnerability
actions.description: In one instance, the actors attempted impersonation of the domain controller, likely by exploiting Microsoft’s Netlogon (also known as “Zerologon”) privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2020-1472).

actions.name: use living off the land techniques to gather information about domain controllers, trusted domains, and admin groups
actions.description: The actors leverage living off the land (LOTL) to gain knowledge about the target systems and internal networks using Windows command-line tools.

actions.name: use Nltest and Net group commands to enumerate domain controllers, trusts, and admin groups
actions.description: The actors used Nltest and Net group commands to enumerate domain controllers, trusted domains, and domain and enterprise administrators.

actions.name: use LDAP query in PowerShell to search Active Directory for computer display names, OS, descriptions, and distinguished names
actions.description: The actors used a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) query in PowerShell to search the AD for computer display names, operating systems, descriptions, and distinguished names.

actions.name: likely made outbound connections to Cobalt Strike Beacon command and control infrastructure using msedge.exe
actions.description: On one occasion, using msedge.exe, the actors likely made outbound connections to Cobalt Strike Beacon command and control (C2) infrastructure.

actions.name: download files related to remote access and organization inventory while logged in to victim accounts
actions.description: In a couple instances, while logged in to victim accounts, the actors downloaded files related to gaining remote access to the organization and to the organization’s inventory, likely exfiltrating the files.
